title: Djibouti boat capsize: Children among 139 dead with 84 still missing, UN says
summary:
At least 139 migrants including 15 children have died and dozens more are still missing after a boat sank off the coast of Djibouti, the UN's migration office has said.
The boat had been travelling from Djibouti to Yemen with 305 people aboard when it capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night.
Around 82 people were rescued, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said.
IOM's Djibouti mission chief Alexandre Coissac called the tragedy a "stark reminder" of the dangers migrants face when seeking a new life elsewhere.
Since 10 September, the IOM said its Displacement Tracking Matrix had observed more than 20,000 "movements" from Ethiopia to Djibouti.

title: I got divorced abroad and decided to stay in Europe. My $900 pension goes so much further in a tiny French village.
summary:
This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Karen Anderson, 57, a Californian who moved to the UK in 2011 and now lives in a small village in northwestern France.
And in 2016, we bought a house in France for €45,000 ($50,450), far less than anything we could have afforded in the UK.
I eventually returned to Europe, but by 2023, my ex-husband and I decided to divorce.
Despite being so small, the village has a restaurant and a church dating back to the 14th or 15th century.
It may look like a dream to other people, but Americans don't always see the sacrifices you make to live abroad.

summary:

title: Nigel Farage says Reform will suspend the UK asylum system for five years and deport thousands of refugees if he becomes PM
summary:
Nigel Farage today pledged to ban anyone from being granted asylum in the UK for five years if Reform wins the next election.
The Reform UK leader re-ignited a proposal from earlier this year to suspend the asylum system for a full parliamentary term and declare void any applications in progress.
All asylum tribunals, legal refugee routes and resettlement schemes will be scrapped and a Reform government would not hear the around 90,000 outstanding asylum and humanitarian protection appeals and instead deport the claimants.
Reform says there is 'no mandate' for such schemes and that anyone who has arrived under them would be deported.
But Reform is now expanding the toolkit of measures for countries that would not be hit hard by such restrictions.
